lines.say: {t3}Three terms of a geometric sequence, {sl}and they all depend on k. {q}It converges. Find k, and the sum to infinity.
Real Edexcel A-level question. {pz}Pause and try it!
{r}Geometric means the same ratio every step, {sq}so the middle squared equals the first times the third.
{ex}Expand, tidy up, {fa}and factorise. {roots}k is twenty, or two thirds.
{k23}Try two thirds: six, ten, sixteen and two thirds. {up}The ratio's five thirds, so it explodes. {no}No good.
{k20}Now twenty: sixty-four, minus forty-eight, thirty-six. {fly}Ratio minus three quarters, so every term shrinks and flips.
{sum}Add them up, and the total zig-zags in. {lim}a over one minus r gives {ans}two hundred and fifty-six sevenths!
{trap}Keep it as a fraction. Thirty-six point six loses the mark.
